frozen_identity.variant: 12 x 3.5-inch common LFF, no bezel, no rear disk module
frozen_identity.installed_configuration: SM211 2xGE, blank photographed PCIe positions, two stacked WEPW80015 460 W AC PSUs, independent left/right shells

before_reproduction.finding: Both engines exposed the same model-side draw-order risk: source cards, procedural face/rear relief, and the full closed core used coplanar or sub-threshold parallel planes. Subtle edge/layer instability was reproducible even though no whole-device disappearance occurred in the 5-degree sample.

root_causes: Canonical face cards and the previous full-size chassis core were coplanar or too closely parallel.
The rear photograph and procedural rear ports/slot covers represented the same surface twice.
Front ear/carrier backing and top latch relief contained competing near-surface planes.
repairs: Inset the watertight core by 1 mm and put canonical face planes on the physical exterior planes.
Removed the duplicate front-ear cap and left source-locked front pixels as the sole face representation.
Replaced the full rear card plus duplicate procedural rear detail with seven non-overlapping source-locked rear regions and stable 0.7 mm backings.
Disabled duplicate procedural rear port/slot surfaces while retaining source-proven cord-loop silhouette geometry.
Moved top latch and carrier backing to stable, non-competing depth levels; no source-locked PNG was regenerated.

standard_and_web.materials: OPAQUE only; baseColor alpha 1; doubleSided false

authenticity_conclusion: PASS_WITH_BOTTOM_FALLBACK: all identity-bearing front/rear/side/top features match the frozen H22M-03 12-LFF delivery configuration. No non-bottom identity gap remains.
warnings_and_residual_risk: The underside remains a deliberately plain, opaque generic material fallback; no unsupported bottom detail is claimed.
Two reported coplanar contacts are each below 1 mm^2 and belong to solid cord-loop joints; they are not visible draw-order surfaces.
